features.text: The patient is 62 years old and female.
The patient experienced a recent heart attack and had another stent placed.
The patient had chest pain that started a couple of weeks ago and was described as intense and crushing.
The chest pain did not improve with rest.
The patient did not experience shortness of breath or dizziness with the chest pain.
The patient has swelling in her legs, which started after hospital discharge and is worse in the right leg.
The leg swelling is pitting and does not improve throughout the day.
The patient has been taking her prescribed medications as directed and has not missed any doses.
The patient has a reduced ejection fraction of 35% and moderate mitral regurgitation.
The patient had an angiogram performed when the new stent was placed.
The patient was told that a stent was placed in a coronary artery due to a blockage, but specific details about the number, location, or severity of the blockage were not provided.
The patient does not have specific details about recent blood tests, including troponin levels, BNP, or renal function tests.
The patient has been walking her dog daily and has not been completely inactive.
